review: Frozen seven-module full-star selection and quotient-minor component
summary: The exact seven-module batch constructs a maximum finite assignment, proves genuine alternating reassignment with an exact one-leaf gain, selects a nonempty full induced-star family when A is nonempty, bounds its actual outside B-neighbors, and constructs its genuine width-(ell+1) simple quotient minor. No maximum-packing, route-existence, reassignment, cardinal-gain or minor-model oracle appears in the endpoint hypotheses. This is a component semantic pass only.

source_reference.correspondence: For the source domain ell>=1 and disjoint partition (A,B), each selected branch is an actual induced ell-star. Its selected vertices intersect B exactly in C, so the proved B\C boundary bound is the source B\V(F) bound. The finite-assignment construction permits empty assignments at unused candidate centers; these are not asserted to be nonempty source ell-minus-star components. All selected centers in the final source application have exactly ell>=1 leaves.
source_reference.proof_organization: Directed closure and loop erasure give a rigorous route to the endpoint without assuming the printed path-extension assertions. Compatibility is proved locally against all original leaves of a destination star, and distinct centers ensure the later dynamic exchanges retain those same destination leaves. This review certifies the resulting endpoint, not a separate theorem identifying the custom route predicate with every detail of the paper global triangle-free alternating-path definition.

exact_endpoint.name: MinorFreeSpanners.exists_full_star_minor
inputs: Finite vertex type V with DecidableEq; G is a SimpleGraph V
A and B are Finsets with Disjoint A B
ell, dA, dB are natural numbers
ell * B.card <= A.card and dA < dB
Every x in A has at most dA actual adjacent vertices in A
Every x in A has at least dB actual adjacent vertices in B
outputs: C subset B and a literal assignment L : V -> Finset V supported only at C
Each assigned leaf lies in A and is adjacent to its center; the leaves of each star are independent, and different centers have disjoint leaf sets
Exactly ell leaves at each selected center
Every selected leaf has at most dA actual neighbors in B minus C
The literal union of center-plus-leaf branches has exactly (ell+1)*C.card vertices
An actual MinorModel of starPackingQuotient G C L in G with every branch cardinality at most ell+1

findings.detail: IsStarPacking explicitly enforces zero assignments outside B, actual A membership, host adjacency, leaf independence, pairwise-disjoint leaf sets and the natural capacity. The maximum is selected from the finite universe of all V-to-Finset-V functions after filtering these actual constraints; the empty assignment supplies nonemptiness. Thus global optimality is derived, not supplied to the final theorem. Literal Function.update insertion requires a globally unused leaf, actual adjacency, compatibility with every existing leaf and spare capacity. The proof checks both orientations of leaf independence and all affected disjointness cases. The union identity is exactly insertion into B.biUnion L, so one-step maximality uses a real cardinal increase.

Leaf deletion preserves all assignment conditions. Pairwise disjointness ensures deleting y at its owner deletes y from the global occupied set exactly. Exchange removes an actual old leaf y, inserts the genuinely unused x and proves the new occupied set is insert x (old union erase y), with y now unused everywhere. Dynamic route induction telescopes these changes: the recursive gain restores y, leaving precisely insert x (original union), hence exactly one additional leaf. Route constructors require only concrete edge, compatibility, old-membership, capacity and simplicity data, never a valid resulting assignment or a pre-established gain. The static route uses the original L throughout. to_dynamic preserves the original assignments at all future centers because the current center is absent from the remaining center list; this supplies all future compatibility, old-membership and terminal-capacity premises. Both side-lists are nodup. vertices_mem plus disjoint A,B prove no vertex is repeated across the two sides either. The final contradiction to maximum size is therefore internal.

Head induction on reflexive-transitive directed reachability produces a chain with the same endpoints. If the new initial vertex is already in the recursively obtained simple chain, the proof keeps the suffix beginning at that vertex; directed adjacency and the old last vertex are preserved. Otherwise it prepends the original directed edge. The proof uses neither symmetry nor a reverse edge. The reflexive case is the singleton chain. No finite-type or path oracle is assumed.

Each center transition is witnessed by an actual leaf of its source star and an actual compatible edge into the destination star, with both centers explicitly in B. A nodup center chain yields an original-packing static route: its outgoing old leaf cannot occur in any future star by leaf disjointness, and the unused incoming leaf cannot occur in the recursively chosen leaf list. The resulting leaf simplicity is derived rather than presumed. Arbitrary directed reachability is reduced to this simple chain; if the final center had spare room, the already-proved static augmentation would contradict the internally obtainable maximum. The actual finite closure starts only at compatible B-centers, its transitions stay in B, and its definition does not silently add noncenters. Saturation follows for every member.

For each conflicting center, choose one actual old leaf adjacent to w. These leaves lie in A, and equality of two chosen leaves would violate disjointness of their distinct owners. The map is therefore an injection from the center subtype to the actual A-neighbor subtype, not a multiplicity or average-degree estimate. If every B-neighbor were blocked, this count would contradict the strict B-neighbor versus A-neighbor gap, producing a real compatible seed. For a selected leaf w and a B-neighbor outside the reachable set, absence of a conflicting destination leaf would provide a real center transition from its reachable owner, placing that neighbor inside the closure. Applying the same injection yields the stated actual outside-neighbor bound.

The theorem selects its maximum assignment internally. In the full-coverage case, exact disjoint-union cardinality and ell*|B|<=|A| force equality of the sum of all individual capacity bounds, so every B-center has exactly ell leaves; the outside boundary is empty. In the other case, covered_subset yields an actual uncovered x in A. The finite compatible-center closure is contained in B and full by the maximum argument. The assignment is literally restricted to those centers, and the proof checks its occupied union is exactly the old assignment union over C. The conflict bound for each selected leaf is then composed with that leaf actual A-degree hypothesis. Strict degree inequalities provide a seed and hence nonempty C; no positive ell assumption or unproved nonempty-family oracle is used.

With disjoint center and leaf domains, branches insert b (L b) are genuinely pairwise disjoint: center-center, both center-leaf orientations and leaf-leaf cases are all handled. Each vertex has an actual host walk of length zero or one to its center, and concatenating one such walk with the reverse of another gives a branch-internal walk of length at most two. branch_adj_iff proves that the host induced on a branch has exactly the center-leaf edges. Looplessness prevents a center being its own leaf. The disjoint biUnion calculation gives exactly (ell+1)*|C| selected vertices for a full family. The quotient vertex type is the actual subtype C; adjacency means distinct centers and an actual crossing host edge. This excludes loops and merges parallel crossings by proposition-valued adjacency. minorModel uses the literal branch finsets, actual internal walks and these crossing edges. Width follows from actual branch cardinality, and the endpoint supplies this model itself.

domain_and_scope_notes: Fintype V is essential to the stated maximum-over-all-assignments construction and finite closure. The source finite simple graph application lies in this domain.
Natural ell,dA,dB include the source nonnegative integer degree parameters. dA<dB implies dB>=1. No positivity condition is lost by using naturals.

For ell=0 every leaf set is empty; selected branches are singletons. If A is nonempty, the strict degree hypothesis still supplies a compatible seed and nonempty selected centers. The boundary assertion is then vacuous because there are no selected leaves. This is a valid extension, not a claim of a nontrivial source claw.

For A empty and ell>=1, the size assumption forces B empty, hence C empty. The endpoint correctly states nonemptiness only conditionally on A.Nonempty. With A empty and ell=0, choosing C=B is allowed and still gives singleton branches.

IsStarPacking alone only makes leaf assignments disjoint; it does not assume A and B disjoint. The stronger selection lemma can use this abstraction. Vertex-disjoint star branches and the final minor correctly require disjoint A,B through the endpoint and branch_disjoint hypotheses.
No global independence of the selected vertex union is asserted. Each individual branch induces a star; arbitrary edges between different branches are allowed and form the quotient edges.

The source partition and B-independence assumptions are stronger than this construction needs. Under disjoint A,B, selected leaves cannot be B vertices, so outside centers B minus C coincide with B outside the whole selected vertex union.

The graph returned is the simple quotient on selected stars after deleting every unselected host vertex. It is not the full G/F contraction retaining unselected singleton branches. No edge-loss or density preservation estimate for that fuller contraction is supplied.

The output is an explicit finite branch family plus an actual SimpleGraph quotient and MinorModel. No separate Lean forest-valued F packaging or equality with the paper named alternating-path predicate is claimed by this endpoint.
The separate Postle Section 5 source concern is outside this review; this report makes no theorem-refutation claim about it.
